evidence.title: Hoya sole vendor with validated High-NA EUV blanks
evidence.excerpt: As of Q1 2025, Hoya is understood to be the only vendor with validated blank products for High-NA EUV systems—critical for logic nodes below 2 nm.

evidence.title: Hoya dominance exceeds 75% in EUV mask blanks volume and qualification
evidence.excerpt: In the narrow but strategically vital segment of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) mask blanks, Hoya's dominance exceeds 75% by volume, and arguably more by technical performance and process qualifications.

evidence.title: High-NA EUV blanks require co-development with ASML scanners
evidence.excerpt: Each generation of EUV mask blanks must be co-developed and co-qualified with ASML's EUV scanner roadmap, which is now progressing from 0.33 NA (numerical aperture) to 0.55 NA High-NA systems. These new systems alter flare sensitivity, substrate topography tolerances, and defect detectability thresholds, rendering legacy mask blanks non-transferable.

evidence.title: AGC capacity expansion for EUVL blanks (not specifically High-NA qualified)
evidence.excerpt: Production will begin in January 2024, and through gradual expansion, the AGC Group's EUVL mask blank production capacity will expand by approximately 30% of the current capacity in 2025. AGC is the world's only manufacturer of EUVL mask blanks that can handle every aspect from 'glass materials' to 'coating'.
evidence.limitations: AGC claims EUVL capability but does NOT mention High-NA qualification status

evidence.title: JX Advanced Metals 50% InP capacity expansion for AI demand
evidence.excerpt: JX Advanced Metals is making a total investment of ¥3.3 billion to increase InP substrate production capacity by about 50% compared to 2025 levels.

evidence.title: 70% InP supply-demand gap: 2M devices vs 600k capacity
evidence.excerpt: The global demand for indium phosphide devices is expected to reach 2 million pieces in 2025, while the production capacity is only 600,000 pieces, with a supply-demand gap as high as 70%. Furthermore, the orders of global leading suppliers are fully booked until 2026.

evidence.title: AXT InP backlog reaches $100M+ in supply-constrained market
evidence.excerpt: backlog of orders and customer forecasts achieving record levels, with the InP backlog reaching over $100 million — described as a 'new high.' In this supply-constrained environment.

evidence.title: AXT InP capacity roadmap: $35M/Q (2026), $65-70M/Q (2027-2028)
evidence.excerpt: they plan to reach $35 million per quarter capability by the end of 2026, then double yet again to $65 million to $70 million of capacity per quarter by 2027-2028.

evidence.title: AXT added 25% InP capacity since Q4 2025
evidence.excerpt: The company added roughly 25% more InP capacity since Q4 2025 and targets reaching $35 million per quarter InP manufacturing capacity by end-2026, scaling to $65–70 million per quarter by end-2027.

evidence.title: Sumitomo Electric 40% InP capacity expansion by 2026
evidence.excerpt: Sumitomo Electric Industries has announced plans to expand its 6-inch InP wafer production capacity by 40% by 2026 to address the booming demand for photonic integrated circuits.

evidence.title: AXT vertical integration advantage: proprietary furnace design and control
evidence.excerpt: AXT's distinctive competitive advantage lies in its internal furnace engineering. The company designs and builds its own crystal growth furnaces internally, which management claims enables both cost control and faster capacity scaling than competitors relying on third-party equipment.

evidence.title: Coherent vertical integration in InP substrates and EML lasers
evidence.excerpt: Coherent benefits from vertical integration across substrates, epitaxy, and EMLs, with strong datacenter momentum. The company designs and manufactures InP-based EMLs and CW lasers, VCSELs, silicon photonics, detectors, and finished transceiver modules in-house.

evidence.title: CDU lead-time normalization suggests easing constraint
evidence.excerpt: CDU lead-time normalization is one of eight specific catalysts being monitored... cooling architecture is the thermal gating factor on how much next-generation compute gets deployed.
evidence.limitations: Normalization language suggests constraint is easing, not currently gating

evidence.title: CDU custom design and integration: 10-12 month lead time
evidence.excerpt: customized rack solutions in existing data centers can entail a construction lag of 10 to 12 months.

evidence.title: Vertiv 45x CDU manufacturing capacity expansion in 2024
evidence.excerpt: Vertiv's 45x expansion of CDU manufacturing capacity in 2024 and Modine's $100 million facility investment directly address this constraint.

evidence.title: CDU market has room for 40+ suppliers, not currently saturated
evidence.excerpt: availability goes beyond hardware—it also requires skilled teams to design, commission, and maintain CDUs across global sites. The DLC market is projected to reach close to $6 billion by 2029, with room for multiple vendors to succeed.

evidence.title: TSMC received ASML High-NA EUV tool in Q4 2024
evidence.excerpt: TSMC received first High NA EUV lithography machine from ASML in Q4 2024. To leverage the new lithography system, chipmakers are simultaneously developing masks, etching processes, resolution-enhancement techniques, and metrology—all of which must be co-optimized.

evidence.title: Intel, TSMC, Samsung all deployed High-NA EUV systems 2023-2025
evidence.excerpt: The three foundries that have received high-NA EUV equipment from ASML are Intel, TSMC, and Samsung. Intel: ASML's TWINSCAN EXE:5000 High-NA EUV system was delivered first to Intel in December 2023. TSMC: later delivered in late 2024. Samsung: Q1 2025.

evidence.title: Nvidia $4B commitment locks out other buyers from EML/InP supply beyond 2027
evidence.excerpt: In March 2026, Nvidia committed $4 billion to Lumentum and Coherent to secure priority access to their EML production, pushing lead times for all other buyers beyond 2027.

evidence.title: Coherent 2x InP capacity increase in Sherman TX and Tarfala Sweden
evidence.excerpt: To address laser supply bottlenecks, Coherent began six-inch InP production in Sherman, Texas, and added a second ramp in Tarfala, Sweden, targeting roughly a 2x internal InP capacity increase over the next year.
